title: Posting the Retiree's Contribution on the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans
content:
On a plan of the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans the retiree's contribution is collected by the method their group contract offers and they chose: deducted from their pension, billed to them directly, taken by bank transfer, or remitted in bulk by the sponsor.

## The condition on posting a payment

No payment entry carrying the same remittance reference and the same amount is already posted on this enrollment.

The plan's own payment records settle this before the money is posted, on the enrollment the payment names. Two payment entries carrying the same remittance reference and the same amount on the same enrollment are the same posting; a different posting date, a different coverage month or a different side of the split makes them different postings.

## Where a pension deduction is being set up

A pension deduction takes the tier's lead months to begin, during which the retiree is billed directly and must keep paying; the plan says so when the deduction is set up rather than letting arrears build.

## The order in which money is applied

Money is posted against the oldest unpaid coverage month first, and within a month against the retiree's own share before the sponsor's.

Stated as an ordering of two questions: the older coverage month is settled before any newer one is touched, and only once the coverage month is fixed does the split within that month arise, where the retiree's own share is settled before the sponsor's.

## A bulk remittance from a sponsor

A bulk remittance from the sponsor is split across the retirees the file names, and a line that names nobody the plan holds is queried with the sponsor rather than posted to the nearest match.

## Money the plan should not keep

An overpayment is refunded by the channel the money arrived on, and a deduction that kept running after cover ended is refunded in full without the retiree having to ask.
